series.name: Procedural Breadth
series.description: Scopes the workflow, decision branching, and step granularity informed by the entity model and relationship graph.

open_ended.text: What is the overall scope of the procedure or workflow? What does it start from and what is its end state?

follow_up_choices.text: Narrow — a single well-defined task with clear boundaries
Moderate — an end-to-end process with several stages
Broad — a multi-phase workflow spanning distinct sub-processes

open_ended.text: How many distinct steps, stages, or phases should the procedure contain? What is the natural breakdown?

follow_up_choices.text: 2–4 steps — quick process with few handoffs
5–8 steps — moderate complexity with clear waypoints
9+ steps — comprehensive procedure with fine-grained stages

open_ended.text: Where are the key decision points, branches, or conditional paths? At which steps must a choice be made that affects the rest of the flow?

follow_up_choices.text: No branching — a single linear path from start to finish
Few branches — 1–2 decision points with 2–3 choices each
Moderate branching — multiple decision points with varying path counts

open_ended.text: What are the expected inputs and outputs at each stage? What data or artifacts flow between steps?

follow_up_choices.text: Simple I/O — each step takes one input and produces one output
Multi-I/O — some steps consume or produce multiple items
Network I/O — steps pass data through a shared context rather than direct handoffs

open_ended.text: What fallback paths, error handling, or recovery procedures should be included for when things go wrong?

follow_up_choices.text: Minimal — errors abort the procedure with a clear message
Retry-based — failed steps can be retried with backoff
Recovery paths — dedicated handling for known failure modes with alternative flows

open_ended.text: How granular should each procedural step be? Should steps be coarse (several actions) or fine (one action per step)?

follow_up_choices.text: Coarse — each step is a meaningful phase (2–5 sub-actions per step)
Fine — each step is a single atomic action
Mixed — core steps are fine; well-established procedures are coarser
